mainTopic: Unloading an animal and צער בעלי חיים; the order of priority among one's own, a teacher's and a father's lost items; who counts as 'his teacher.'
overview: The amud begins with a ברייתא that reads "רובץ תחת משאו" narrowly. It says the duty to unload applies only to an animal lying down right now, not a standing one or a habitual collapser, and only under a load it can bear. The גמרא argues that if צער בעלי חיים were from the Torah, these limits would make no sense. It answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds it is דרבנן, and on loading he agrees with the רבנן. A second ברייתא sets when the duty begins: once you see the animal from within a ריס. The helper then walks along up to a פרסה, and רבה בר בר חנה says he may be paid for that. A new משנה ranks lost items: your own comes first, then your teacher's, then your father's, unless the father is a חכם. The same order applies to unloading burdens and redeeming captives. The גמרא learns 'yours comes first' from "אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון" and warns against always insisting on it. It then debates who counts as 'his teacher,' with stories about רבא, שמואל, עולא, and רב חסדא and רב הונא, and rulings like רבי יהודה or רבי יוסי. The amud ends with a ברייתא ranking מקרא, משנה and תלמוד that seems to contradict itself; רבי יוחנן's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא that limits the duty to unload
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads each word of "רובץ תחת משאו" as a limit on when one must help unload an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Lying down' means an animal lying down now, not one that always lies down. 'Lying down' means not one that is standing. 'Under its burden' means not one that has already been unloaded. 'Under its burden' means a load the animal can normally carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as evidence in its search to find out whether צער בעלי חיים is from the Torah. This step only presents the source. The argument built on it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns four limits from two words of the פסוק. The מצוה does not apply to an animal that habitually collapses, to one that is standing, or to one already unloaded. It also only applies when the load is a normal size the animal can bear. These limits are the raw material for the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that habitually lies down (a 'collapser')

phrases.english: "Lying down," but not a habitual collapser,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is שמות 23:5. A רבצן is an animal that lies down all the time, even without a real reason.

phrases.english: "lying down," but not standing.
"Under its burden," but not unloaded.
"Under its burden": a burden that it is able to bear.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״רֹבֵץ״ וְלֹא רַבְצָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's ongoing search, begun before this section, to prove whether צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא or דרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading "רובץ תחת משאו" narrowly

steps.title: If animal suffering were a Torah law, these limits would make no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that a Torah-level duty to stop animal suffering would apply whether the animal is lying down, habitually collapsing, or standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that preventing animal suffering is a Torah law, what difference does it make to me whether it is lying down, whether it is a habitual collapser, or whether it is standing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא. Its limits suggest that צער בעלי חיים is not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal suffers under its load whether it is lying down, standing, or a habitual collapser. If the Torah required us to prevent that suffering, we would have to unload in all of these cases. Since the ברייתא exempts some of them, it seems to hold that צער בעלי חיים is only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: And if you say that animal suffering is a Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי רוֹבֵץ, וּמָה לִי רַבְצָן,
phrases.english: what is it to me if it is lying down, and what is it to me if it is a habitual collapser,
and what is it to me if it is standing!
phrases.notes: In other words, the animal suffers in every one of these cases, so a Torah law would require helping in all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds the argument out of the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah duty to prevent suffering would not depend on the animal's position or habits, yet the ברייתא makes it depend on them.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that צער בעלי חיים is only דרבנן, so it proves nothing about the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says that preventing animal suffering is only a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the ברייתא reflects only one opinion, so it does not settle the question for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not rejected by explaining the ברייתא differently. Instead, the ברייתא is assigned to a specific תנא, רבי יוסי הגלילי, who already holds צער בעלי חיים is דרבנן. So those who hold it is דאורייתא are not challenged by it.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא,
phrases.english: Whose is this? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי,
who says that animal suffering is a rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the argument of step 2 by assigning the ברייתא to one תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא represents everyone, so צער בעלי חיים must be דרבנן according to all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds צער בעלי חיים is דרבנן; others may still hold it is דאורייתא.

steps.title: Support: 'a burden it can bear' is רבי יוסי הגלילי's idea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer: the ברייתא's line about 'a burden it can bear' is a view known to belong to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the ברייתא teaches that 'under its burden' means a load the animal can bear. Who do we know holds this idea? רבי יוסי הגלילי. So learn from it that the ברייתא is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from inside the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth line of the ברייתא, which limits the מצוה to a normal load, matches an idea the גמרא says belongs to רבי יוסי הגלילי. That detail shows the ברייתא was written by him. So the answer in step 3 is not just a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (a supporting proof)

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since it teaches: "Under its burden"
means a burden that it is able to bear.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאִית לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא –
phrases.english: Whom have you heard who holds this reasoning?
רבי יוסי הגלילי. Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the attribution made in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own line: "a burden it is able to bear"

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא matches the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the attribution: the line 'not unloaded' must mean loading is only required for pay, and that is the view of the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say this follows רבי יוסי הגלילי? The later part says 'under its burden' but not one already unloaded. What does that mean? If it means there is no duty at all, the Torah says 'you shall surely lift them with him'! So it must mean you do not have to load it for free, only for pay. Who holds that? The רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from steps 3–4 using a different line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a separate Torah מצוה to help load an animal, so 'not unloaded' cannot mean no obligation at all. It must mean unloading is free but loading is done for pay. That split is the known view of the רבנן, which suggests the ברייתא is theirs and not רבי יוסי הגלילי's.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall surely lift up with him (the מצוה of loading)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different מצוות here: פריקה (unloading, "עזוב תעזוב") and טעינה (loading back up, "הקם תקים"). 'Not unloaded' refers to an animal whose load is already off, so the only remaining help is loading.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי?
phrases.english: And can you establish it according to רבי יוסי הגלילי?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: ״תַּחַת מַשָּׂאוֹ״ – וְלֹא מְפוֹרָק.
phrases.english: But it teaches in the latter part: "Under its burden," but not unloaded.
What does "not unloaded" mean?
If you say an unloaded animal gets no help at all,
but it is written: "You shall surely lift up with him"!
Rather, it is obvious: an unloaded animal is not helped for free,
but only for payment.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאִית לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא – רַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: Whom have you heard who holds this reasoning? The רבנן!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution to רבי יוסי הגלילי made in steps 3–4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's ruling on loading (only for pay) is the רבנן's view, so the ברייתא seems to be the רבנן's and not רבי יוסי הגלילי's.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees with the רבנן about loading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really is רבי יוסי הגלילי; on loading he simply holds like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is רבי יוסי הגלילי, and on loading he agrees with the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps its attribution to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Matching the רבנן on one point does not mean the ברייתא must be theirs. רבי יוסי הגלילי can hold his own view on צער בעלי חיים and on 'a burden it can bear,' and still agree with the רבנן that loading is for pay. So the ברייתא fits him completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Loading (helping put the load back on)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that limits unloading to an animal that is lying down, not standing, and carrying a normal load follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds צער בעלי חיים is דרבנן. On loading for pay he agrees with the רבנן. So this ברייתא cannot prove that צער בעלי חיים is דרבנן according to everyone.

phrases.english: Actually, it is רבי יוסי הגלילי,
and regarding loading, he holds like the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and confirms the attribution of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: one תנא can agree with another on a separate point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the loading rule is the רבנן's, the whole ברייתא must be the רבנן's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי יוסי הגלילי's; he agrees with the רבנן only about loading.

steps.title: Two verses set the range: not too far, not only a direct encounter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא balances 'כי תראה' (if you see) against 'כי תפגע' (if you encounter) to show the obligation applies at a middle distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'If you see.' You might think this means even from far away, so the Torah says 'If you encounter.' But if it only said 'If you encounter,' you might think you must actually bump into it, so the Torah says 'If you see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about when you become obligated to help an animal that has fallen under its load. It uses two different words from the פסוקים so that each one limits the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seeing' alone could mean even from very far away, and 'encountering' alone could mean only when you are right next to it. Putting the two words together means the obligation starts when you see the animal from fairly close. The next step tells us exactly how close.

keyTerms.meaning: An encounter, meeting up with something

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"If you see"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:5, the פסוק about helping unload a fallen donkey.

phrases.english: one might think even from far away,
so the verse says: "If you encounter."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:4, the פסוק just before it.

phrases.english: If it said only "If you encounter,"
one might think it requires an actual encounter?
so the verse says: "If you see."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כִּי תִרְאֶה״ – יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ מֵרָחוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the debate over who the ברייתא follows to a new ברייתא about the distance at which the duty begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The obligation to unload applies neither from any distance nor only at actual contact; it applies at a middle distance.

steps.title: The Sages measure the distance: a ריס
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines 'seeing that counts as encountering' as 2/15 of a מיל, which is called a ריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what kind of seeing counts as an encounter? The חכמים estimated it as one part out of seven and a half of a מיל, and that is a ריס.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives an exact distance for the middle range it just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One out of seven and a half' means you divide a מיל into seven and a half equal parts and take one of them, which is 2/15 of a מיל. That distance is called a ריס. If you see the animal from within a ריס, you are obligated to help.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages estimated, setting a fixed measure
A distance of 2/15 of a מיל

steps.confusionAlert: 'One of seven and a half' is not 7.5 מיל. It is a small fraction of one מיל, 2/15 of it.

phrases.english: And what is a seeing
that has an element of encounter in it?
The Sages estimated it as
one part out of seven and a half of a mil,
and that is a ris.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא רְאִיָּיה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ פְּגִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the general middle range from step 7 into an exact measurement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The obligation starts when one sees the animal from within a ריס, which is 2/15 of a מיל.

steps.title: After reloading, walk with the animal up to a פרסה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the helper walks along with the animal for up to a פרסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: and he walks along with it up to a פרסה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא adds what the helper does after the load is back on: he goes along with the animal for some distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping does not stop the moment the load is back on. The helper keeps the owner and animal company for up to a פרסה. The next step asks whether he may charge for this.

keyTerms.meaning: A distance unit, much longer than a ריס

phrases.english: It was taught:
and he walks along with it up to a parasang.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וּמִדַּדֶּה עִמּוֹ עַד פַּרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further duty that follows the unloading and loading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The helper accompanies the animal for up to a פרסה.

steps.title: He may take payment for walking along
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says that the person who escorts the animal may charge for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: and he takes payment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה adds a detail to the ברייתא: the walking along is paid work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he may take payment, walking along is not part of the free מצוה of unloading. It is an extra service, so the helper may charge for his time.
steps.whatToRemember: The duty to help begins within a ריס, the helper walks with the animal up to a פרסה, and he may be paid for that walking.

phrases.english: Rabbah bar bar Chana said:
And he takes payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: וְנוֹטֵל שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the ברייתא in step 9 by saying the escorting is paid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Escorting the animal up to a פרסה is done for pay.

steps.title: Your own lost item comes before your father's or your teacher's
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if you can only save one lost item, your own comes first over your father's and over your teacher's.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: His lost item and his father's lost item: his own comes first. His lost item and his teacher's lost item: his own comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with someone who can only take care of one of two lost items, and tells him which one comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a conflict: two lost items, and time or ability for only one. The משנה says your own loss comes first, even over the loss of your father or your teacher. It gives no reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
His lost item and his father's lost item:
his own lost item comes first.
His lost item and his teacher's lost item:
his own comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֲבֵדָתוֹ וַאֲבֵדַת אָבִיו – אֲבֵדָתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic: priority among lost items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's own lost item takes priority over his father's and over his teacher's.

steps.title: Teacher before father, because the teacher brings him to עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: Between a father's and a teacher's lost item, the teacher's comes first, because Torah learning brings a person to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father's lost item and his teacher's lost item: his teacher's comes first. His father brought him into this world, but his teacher, who taught him wisdom, brings him to the life of עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares the father with the teacher and explains why the teacher comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning compares two gifts. A father gives life in this world, while a Torah teacher gives a way into עולם הבא, which is greater. So the teacher's loss is handled first.

keyTerms.meaning: The life of the World to Come

phrases.english: His father's lost item and his teacher's lost item:
his teacher's comes first,
because his father brought him into this world,
but his teacher, who taught him wisdom,
brings him to the life of the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבֵדַת אָבִיו וַאֲבֵדַת רַבּוֹ – שֶׁל רַבּוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order of priority, now comparing the father and the teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher's lost item comes before a father's, because Torah teaching brings a person to עולם הבא.

steps.title: A father who is a חכם comes first
steps.stepSummary: If the father is himself a Torah scholar, his lost item comes before the teacher's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if his father is a חכם, his father's lost item comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to the rule that the teacher comes before the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher came first because of his Torah. When the father is also a חכם, he has that same Torah greatness and is also the father, so the usual order is reversed.
steps.whatToRemember: Order of priority: your own lost item first, then your teacher's, then your father's. But a father who is a חכם comes before the teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up the גמרא's coming discussion about how much a person must give up his own interests for others, and how a teacher is defined.

phrases.english: And if his father is a Torah scholar,
his father's comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָבִיו חָכָם – שֶׁל אָבִיו קוֹדֶמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 12 for a father who is a Torah scholar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who is a חכם takes priority over the teacher.

steps.title: Burdens: help the teacher put his down first
steps.stepSummary: If both his father and his teacher are carrying heavy loads, he first helps his teacher put his load down, and then his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his father and his teacher were carrying a burden, he puts down his teacher's first, and afterward puts down his father's.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same order from the lost-item case for a new case: helping someone put down a heavy load.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11–13 dealt with lost items. Here the same rule, teacher before father, is applied to helping with a burden. The teacher still comes first because of the Torah he taught.

phrases.english: If his father and his teacher
were carrying a burden,
he puts down his teacher's

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַנִּיחַ אֶת שֶׁל אָבִיו.
phrases.english: and afterward puts down his father's.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה אָבִיו וְרַבּוֹ נוֹשְׂאִין מַשּׂאוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the teacher-before-father order to a new case: unloading burdens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When unloading burdens, the teacher's load comes before the father's.

steps.title: Captivity: redeem the teacher first
steps.stepSummary: If both his father and his teacher are held captive, he redeems his teacher first and then his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his father and his teacher were in captivity, he redeems his teacher first, and afterward redeems his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same order to the most serious case: freeing people who are held captive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in a matter of a person's freedom, and not only property, the teacher still comes before the father. This shows how highly the משנה values the one who taught you Torah.

phrases.english: If his father and his teacher
were in captivity,
he redeems his teacher
and afterward redeems his father.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה אָבִיו וְרַבּוֹ בְּבֵית הַשְּׁבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same order from burdens to redeeming captives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When redeeming captives, the teacher is redeemed before the father.

steps.title: If the father is a scholar, redeem the father first
steps.stepSummary: If the father is a חכם, the order flips: he redeems his father first, then his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if his father is a Torah scholar, he redeems his father first, and afterward redeems his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the exception: when the father is himself a חכם, he goes ahead of the teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the lost-item exception in step 13. Once the father also has Torah greatness, the reason for putting the teacher first no longer outweighs the father's honor.

phrases.english: And if his father is a scholar,
he redeems his father
and afterward redeems his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָבִיו חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exception to step 15, just as step 13 did for lost items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who is a חכם is redeemed before the teacher.
steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases (lost items, burdens, captivity) the teacher comes before the father, unless the father is a חכם.

steps.title: What is the source for 'your own comes first'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where we learn the משנה's first rule, that your own lost item comes before everyone else's.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these matters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to the first rule in step 11, that your own lost item comes before your father's and your teacher's. The גמרא wants a Torah source for putting yourself first.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From where do we know these things? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: גמרא
From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the very first rule of the משנה, that your own lost item comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by asking for the source of the משנה's first ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a person's own loss takes priority.

steps.title: Source: 'There shall be no needy among you'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב brings the פסוק 'אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון': yours comes before anyone else's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The verse says, 'Only so that there shall be no needy among you.' This teaches that yours comes before anyone else's.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question with a פסוק, which teaches that your own property comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as an instruction to make sure that you yourself do not become poor. So when saving your own loss competes with saving someone else's, protecting your own comes first.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The verse says:
"Only so that there shall be no needy among you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:4. He reads it as: make sure that YOU don't end up needy.

phrases.english: yours comes before anyone else's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון' teaches that one's own property comes first.

steps.title: Warning: always putting yourself first leads to poverty
steps.stepSummary: רב adds that someone who always insists on this rule will end up poor himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who always holds himself to this rule will in the end come to that very state.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a warning to the rule he just taught: don't use it all the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law allows you to put yourself first, but someone who always does so, and never gives up a little for others, will in the end become the needy person himself. So the rule stays in place, but it should be used with generosity.

keyTerms.meaning: Who keeps it for himself (always insists on it)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not taking back the rule from step 18. The law stays the same; he is warning against being too strict about one's own benefit every single time.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who always holds himself to this,
phrases.notes: 'This' means always putting his own things first, even over other people's losses.

phrases.english: will in the end come to that.
phrases.notes: He means he will end up needy himself, the very thing the פסוק wanted to prevent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמְקַיֵּים בְּעַצְמוֹ כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a warning about how to use the rule taught in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who always insists on putting his own property first will end up poor.
steps.whatToRemember: Your own lost item comes first by law (from 'אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון'), but someone who always insists on it may end up needy himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a legal right is not always the best way to act; the גמרא encourages going beyond the strict law.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: 'His teacher' means one who taught him deep understanding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's 'teacher' and brings a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says it means the teacher who taught him חכמה, not one who taught him מקרא and משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'If his father and his teacher were carrying a burden,' and so on. The Rabbis taught: The 'teacher' they spoke about is the teacher who taught him wisdom, not the teacher who taught him Bible and משנה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks who counts as 'his teacher.' A ברייתא begins with רבי מאיר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every teacher gets this special priority over a father. For רבי מאיר, only the teacher who gave him deep understanding of Torah (חכמה) counts. Teaching basic text, like מקרא or משנה, is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Wisdom: deep understanding of Torah and the reasons behind it

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה אָבִיו וְרַבּוֹ נוֹשְׂאִין מַשּׂאוֹי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "If his father and his teacher were carrying a burden," etc.
The Rabbis taught:
The 'teacher' that they spoke of
is his teacher who taught him wisdom,
and not his teacher who taught him Bible and משנה;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רַבּוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹ שֶׁלִּמְּדוֹ חׇכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to define the word 'his teacher.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, only the teacher who taught him חכמה gets priority.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The one he learned most of his knowledge from
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says 'his teacher' is whoever taught him most of his knowledge, whatever the subject.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Anyone from whom he learned most of his knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא: what matters is how much he learned from this teacher, not what kind of learning it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר looked at the type of learning. רבי יהודה looks at the amount: the main teacher is the one who gave him most of his Torah, even if it was מקרא or משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Anyone from whom he learned most of his knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁרוֹב חׇכְמָתוֹ הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר: the test is the amount learned, not the type.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, 'his teacher' is the one he learned most of his Torah from.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Even one משנה makes him your teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that even someone who explained just one משנה to him counts as his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even if he only opened his eyes in one משנה, that is his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The third and broadest opinion: even a small amount of real understanding makes someone your teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר required deep learning, and רבי יהודה required most of one's learning. רבי יוסי requires only that the teacher made even one משנה clear to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He lit up his eyes (made something clear to him)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even if he did not enlighten his eyes
except in one משנה,
that is his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא הֵאִיר עֵינָיו אֶלָּא בְּמִשְׁנָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the broadest definition, after רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, anyone who made even one משנה clear to him is his teacher.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on who is 'his teacher': רבי מאיר says one who taught him חכמה (deep understanding); רבי יהודה says one who taught him most of his knowledge; רבי יוסי says even one who explained a single משנה.

steps.title: רבא's example: רב סחורה explained one word
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a personal example of a teacher who taught him only a single term: רב סחורה explained 'זוהמא ליסטרון' to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: An example is רב סחורה, who explained to me what 'זוהמא ליסטרון' means.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is giving a real example of רבי יוסי's idea that even someone who explained one small thing counts as your teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי (step 22) said that explaining even one משנה makes someone your teacher. רבא shows this in his own life: one word explained by רב סחורה was enough for him to treat רב סחורה as his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: A tool with a spoon at one end and a fork at the other, mentioned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rava said:
For example, Rav Sechora,
who explained to me 'zuhama listeron.'
phrases.notes: This is a word from a משנה in כלים: a tool with a spoon on one end and a fork on the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן רַב סְחוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבי יוסי's view from step 22 with a real example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who explained even one term to you is considered your teacher.

steps.title: שמואל tore his garment for a scholar who explained one משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tore his clothing in mourning for a scholar who had explained to him one line of a משנה about the Temple keys.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל tore his garment when a certain scholar died, because that scholar had explained to him the line: 'One key goes down to the armpit, and one opens directly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example: שמואל mourned like a student for someone who taught him only one line of a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing a garment is what a student does when his teacher dies. שמואל did this for someone who taught him just one explanation, which matches רבי יוסי's view that even one משנה makes someone a teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: He tore his garment (a sign of mourning)

phrases.english: Shmuel tore his garment
over a certain one of the Rabbis
who had explained to him
"One goes down to the armpit
and one opens directly."
phrases.notes: This line is from a משנה in תמיד about two keys used to open the doors into the היכל each morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל קְרַע מָאנֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example, alongside רבא's, of treating a one-time explainer as a teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל treated someone who explained one line of a משנה as his teacher, even mourning him.

steps.title: עולא: Babylonian scholars honor each other, but lost items go only to the main teacher
steps.stepSummary: עולא says Babylonian scholars stand up and tear garments for each other, but for putting a teacher's lost item before a father's, only a main teacher counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The Torah scholars in Babylonia stand up for one another and tear their garments when one of them dies. But when it comes to returning a lost item before their father's, they do this only for their main teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא separates two kinds of honor: general respect, which Babylonian scholars give each other freely, and the lost-item priority, which is only for a main teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The examples of רבא and שמואל might suggest that anyone who taught you something gets full teacher status. עולא limits this: honor like standing and tearing can go wide, but putting a teacher's loss ahead of your father's needs a רבו מובהק.

keyTerms.meaning: Stand up out of respect for
His main teacher, the one he learned most from

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying Babylonian scholars ignore each other's lost items. He means only that the special rule of putting a teacher before a father applies only to the main teacher.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The Torah scholars who are in Babylonia
stand up for one another,
and tear their garments over one another.
But regarding a lost item when his father's is also lost,
they return first only to their main teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the examples of steps 23-24: general honor is broad, but lost-item priority is only for the main teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost-item priority over one's father applies only to one's רבו מובהק.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks about a student whose teacher needs him
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב הונא: what is the law for a student whose teacher also needs him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked רב הונא: If there is a student whose teacher needs him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא raises a new question about the teacher category, setting up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a student becomes so strong that the teacher learns from him too. רב חסדא wants to know whether such a teacher still counts as the student's 'teacher' for getting his lost item returned first.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question of law)

phrases.aramaic: קָבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda asked Rav Huna:
A student whose teacher needs him, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means a student good enough that his teacher learns from him as a study partner.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the edge of the 'teacher' category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a teacher who depends on his student still get teacher priority for lost items?

steps.title: רב הונא answers sharply, taking it personally
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא thinks רב חסדא means the two of them and replies that he does not need רב חסדא; רב חסדא needs him for forty years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: Chisda, Chisda, I don't need you! You need me for forty years.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא replies, but instead of answering the legal question he reacts as if רב חסדא were talking about their own relationship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא was רב הונא's student and also his study partner. רב הונא heard the question as a hint that he needed רב חסדא, so he pushed back hard. The legal question is left without a clear answer.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as the הלכה answer to the question. רב הונא is reacting to what he thought was a personal hint, as the next step shows.

phrases.english: He said to him: Chisda, Chisda,
I do not need you;

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ צְרִיכַתְּ לִי עַד אַרְבְּעִין שְׁנִין.
phrases.english: you need me for forty years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חִסְדָּא חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב חסדא's question, but on a personal level rather than a legal one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No legal ruling; רב הונא rejects the idea that he needs רב חסדא.

steps.title: The falling-out and the forty fasts
steps.stepSummary: The two became upset and stopped visiting each other. Each fasted forty fasts: רב חסדא for hurting רב הונא, and רב הונא for wrongly suspecting רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They became upset with each other and did not visit each other. רב חסדא fasted forty fasts because רב הונא had been hurt. רב הונא fasted forty fasts because he had suspected רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story, showing how both rabbis regretted the misunderstanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא regretted that his question hurt his teacher, even though he didn't mean it that way. רב הונא regretted that he had wrongly read a hidden insult into an honest question. Both took responsibility.

phrases.english: They became upset with each other
and did not go in to visit each other.
Rav Chisda observed forty fasts,
because Rav Huna's feelings were hurt.
Rav Huna observed forty fasts,
because he had suspected Rav Chisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּפַדוּ אַהֲדָדֵי וְלָא עָיְילִי לְגַבֵּי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun by the question and sharp reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both rabbis repented for the misunderstanding with forty fasts each.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: your teacher is the one who taught you most of your learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the three opinions of the ברייתא and brings a ruling: like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה (step 21) said 'his teacher' is the one who taught him most of his knowledge. According to this ruling, someone who explained just one משנה does not get priority over your father.

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: Back in step 21, רבי יהודה said your teacher is whoever taught you most of your knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to the ברייתא's dispute and gives a ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלכה like רבי יהודה: the teacher is the one who taught most of one's knowledge.

steps.title: רב ששת: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הונא reports in the name of רב ששת that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: even one who explained a single משנה is a teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב הונא said in the name of רב ששת: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: A second tradition gives the opposite ruling, so the הלכה is left as a dispute between two traditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי (step 22) said even someone who explained one משנה counts as your teacher. So רבי יוחנן's tradition gives priority only to the main teacher, while רב ששת's tradition gives it even for one explanation.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on 'his teacher': רבי מאיר (who taught him חכמה), רבי יהודה (who taught him most), רבי יוסי (even one משנה). רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה; רב ששת rules like רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing ruling to step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלכה like רבי יוסי: even one who explained one משנה is a teacher.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה on who counts as 'his teacher' is reported in two conflicting traditions: like רבי יהודה or like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really rule like רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה. רבי יוחנן also holds that the law follows an unnamed משנה, and our unnamed משנה only says 'his teacher who taught him wisdom.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? Doesn't רבי יוחנן say the law follows an unnamed משנה? And our משנה says: 'his teacher who taught him wisdom.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ruling from Step 29. It quotes another rule of רבי יוחנן that seems to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's general rule is that the law follows an unnamed משנה (סתם משנה). Our משנה names no author and simply says 'the teacher who taught him wisdom,' which sounds like רבי מאיר's wording, not רבי יהודה's 'most of his learning.' So ruling like רבי יהודה seems to break רבי יוחנן's own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say...? This opens a challenge.
But didn't he say...? This brings a clashing statement.
An unnamed משנה, stated without any author

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say that?
phrases.notes: 'That' is the ruling from Step 29: the law follows רבי יהודה, so your teacher is the one who taught you most of your learning.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The law follows an unnamed Mishnah,
and we learned: his teacher who taught him wisdom.
phrases.notes: This is the wording of our own משנה. It names no author, and it sounds like רבי מאיר's opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 29 by setting it against another rule of the same אמורא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the law follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules like an unnamed משנה, and our unnamed משנה's wording ('taught him wisdom') matches רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה

steps.title: 'Wisdom' means most of his wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the word 'wisdom' in the משנה means 'most of his wisdom,' so the unnamed משנה actually agrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'wisdom' mean? Most of his wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's word 'wisdom' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'wisdom' means 'most of his wisdom,' then the unnamed משנה is saying exactly what רבי יהודה says. Now רבי יוחנן's two rules fit together, and the ruling like רבי יהודה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of his wisdom (most of his learning)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, 'your teacher' (for the laws of lost objects) is the one who taught you most of your Torah learning. The unnamed משנה is read to agree with this.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'wisdom'?
Most of his wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״חׇכְמָה״? רוֹב חׇכְמָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unnamed משנה's 'wisdom' means the deep understanding of Torah (not מקרא or משנה) that רבי מאיר requires, so the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Wisdom' means most of his wisdom, so the unnamed משנה matches רבי יהודה and רבי יוחנן is consistent

steps.title: Ranking the study of מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares three kinds of Torah study. מקרא is a virtue but not a full one, משנה is a virtue that earns reward, and תלמוד is the greatest virtue. Yet it adds: always run to משנה more than to תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Those who study מקרא have a virtue that is not quite a virtue. Those who study משנה have a virtue and get reward for it. Those who study תלמוד have no greater virtue than that. And always run to משנה more than to תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the value of different kinds of Torah learning. It connects to the earlier topic of what kind of teaching makes someone your teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up a ladder: מקרא is lowest, משנה is in the middle, and תלמוד is highest. Its last line seems to reverse the order by telling you to put more effort into משנה. That tension is what the next step will raise.

keyTerms.meaning: The written Torah (the verses of תנ״ך)
Analysis of the משנה: the reasons and the reasoning behind the laws
Be running toward, put your effort into

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Those who engage in Bible study –
it is a virtue and yet not a virtue,
in Mishnah – it is a virtue
and they receive reward for it,

phrases.aramaic: בַּתַּלְמוּד – אֵין לָךְ מִדָּה גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ,
phrases.english: in Talmud – you have no virtue greater than this,
and always run to the Mishnah
more than to the Talmud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָעוֹסְקִין בְּמִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining 'your teacher' by his teaching to a ברייתא about the value of each kind of learning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא is a partial virtue, משנה is a virtue that earns reward, and תלמוד is the greatest. Still, always run more to משנה than to תלמוד.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא calls תלמוד the greatest virtue but then says to run more to משנה. רבי יוחנן begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is itself difficult. You said nothing is greater than תלמוד, and then you said always run to משנה more than to תלמוד! רבי יוחנן said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a contradiction inside the same ברייתא. It then sets up רבי יוחנן's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תלמוד is the highest virtue, it makes no sense to tell people to put more effort into משנה. The beginning and the end of the ברייתא seem to pull in opposite directions. רבי יוחנן is introduced to settle this.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult: a source that contradicts itself

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against an earlier אמורא. The problem is inside the ברייתא itself: its first line and its last line clash.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult.
You said that in Talmud
you have no virtue greater than this,
and then you said:
and always run to the Mishnah
more than to the Talmud!
Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גוּפַאּ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא from Step 33 by setting its first line against its last
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ranking of תלמוד against משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls תלמוד the greatest virtue yet tells you to put more effort into משנה, which is a self-contradiction
